claims.text: Most recurrent genital herpes is caused by HSV-2; an estimated 11.9% of people aged 14 to 49 in the US are infected (about 12%)
claims.quote: Most cases of recurrent genital herpes are caused by HSV-2 ... 11.9% of persons aged 14–49 years are estimated to be infected in the United States

claims.text: First-episode regimens: acyclovir 400 mg three times daily, famciclovir 250 mg three times daily, or valacyclovir 1 g twice daily, each for 7 to 10 days
claims.quote: Acyclovir 400 mg orally 3 times/day for 7–10 days ... Famciclovir 250 mg orally 3 times/day for 7–10 days ... Valacyclovir 1 gm orally 2 times/day for 7–10 days

claims.text: Acyclovir 200 mg five times daily is effective but not recommended because of dosing frequency
claims.quote: Acyclovir 200 mg orally five times/day is also effective but is not recommended because of the frequency of dosing.

claims.text: Treatment can be extended if healing is incomplete after 10 days
claims.quote: Treatment can be extended if healing is incomplete after 10 days of therapy.

claims.text: IV acyclovir 5 to 10 mg/kg every 8 hours for severe disease or complications needing hospitalization (disseminated infection, pneumonitis, hepatitis) or CNS complications (meningitis, encephalitis)
claims.quote: Intravenous (IV) acyclovir therapy (5–10 mg/kg body weight IV every 8 hours) should be provided ... (e.g., disseminated infection, pneumonitis, or hepatitis) ... or CNS complications (e.g., meningitis or encephalitis)

claims.text: Suppressive therapy reduces recurrences by 70% to 80% in people with frequent outbreaks (key takeaways)
claims.quote: Suppressive therapy reduces frequency of genital herpes recurrences by 70%–80% among patients who have frequent recurrences

claims.text: CDC suppressive regimens: acyclovir 400 mg twice daily, valacyclovir 500 mg once daily, valacyclovir 1 g once daily, famciclovir 250 mg twice daily
claims.quote: Acyclovir 400 mg orally 2 times/day ... Valacyclovir 500 mg orally once a day ... Valacyclovir 1 gm orally once a day ... Famciclovir 250 mg orally 2 times/day

claims.text: Valacyclovir 500 mg once daily might be less effective for people with 10 or more episodes a year
claims.quote: Valacyclovir 500 mg once a day might be less effective than other valacyclovir or acyclovir dosing regimens ... for persons who have frequent recurrences (i.e., ≥10 episodes/year).

claims.text: Episodic regimens (acyclovir, valacyclovir): acyclovir 800 mg twice daily x5 d or three times daily x2 d; valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily x3 d or 1 g daily x5 d
claims.quote: Acyclovir 800 mg orally 2 times/day for 5 days ... Acyclovir 800 mg orally 3 times/day for 2 days ... Valacyclovir 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 3 days ... Valacyclovir 1 gm orally once daily for 5 days

claims.text: Episodic regimens (famciclovir): 1 g twice daily x1 d, 500 mg once then 250 mg twice daily x2 d, or 125 mg twice daily x5 d
claims.quote: Famciclovir 1 gm orally 2 times/day for 1 day ... Famciclovir 500 mg once, followed by 250 mg 2 times/day for 2 days ... Famciclovir 125 mg 2 times/day for 5 days

claims.text: Episodic therapy most effective within 1 day of lesion onset or during prodrome; start as soon as symptoms begin; antivirals at onset shorten outbreaks
claims.quote: Episodic treatment of recurrent herpes is most effective if therapy is initiated within 1 day of lesion onset or during the prodrome that precedes some outbreaks.

claims.text: Patients should be given a supply of the drug or a prescription to start treatment immediately when symptoms begin
claims.quote: The patient should be provided with a supply of drug or a prescription for the medication

claims.text: CDC recommends suppressive therapy from 36 weeks for women with recurrent genital herpes: acyclovir 400 mg three times daily or valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily
claims.quote: Acyclovir 400 mg orally 3 times/day ... Valacyclovir 500 mg orally 2 times/day ... Treatment recommended starting at 36 weeks' gestation.

claims.text: Acyclovir believed safe in all trimesters; valacyclovir prenatal data more limited
claims.quote: believed to be safe for use during all trimesters of pregnancy ... data regarding prenatal exposure to valacyclovir and famciclovir are limited

claims.text: Acyclovir is believed to be safe during breastfeeding
claims.quote: Acyclovir is also believed to be safe during breastfeeding.

claims.text: HIV daily suppression: acyclovir 400-800 mg 2-3 times daily, famciclovir 500 mg twice daily, valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily
claims.quote: Acyclovir 400–800 mg orally 2-3 times/day ... Famciclovir 500 mg orally 2 times/day ... Valacyclovir 500 mg orally 2 times/day

claims.text: HIV episodic: acyclovir 400 mg three times daily, famciclovir 500 mg twice daily, valacyclovir 1 g twice daily, each 5 to 10 days
claims.quote: Acyclovir 400 mg orally 3 times/day for 5–10 days ... Famciclovir 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 5–10 days ... Valacyclovir 1 gm orally 2 times/day for 5–10 days

claims.text: Cesarean delivery when recurrent lesions are present at the onset of labor (key takeaways)
claims.quote: women with recurrent genital herpetic lesions at the onset of labor should have a cesarean delivery

claims.text: Recurrences become less frequent over time for many people
claims.quote: frequency of genital HSV-2 recurrence diminishes over time for many persons

claims.text: Majority of HSV-2 infections undiagnosed; most transmitted by people unaware of infection or asymptomatic at transmission
claims.quote: The majority of persons infected with HSV-2 have not had the condition diagnosed ... shed virus intermittently ... most genital herpes infections are transmitted by persons unaware that they have the infection or who are asymptomatic when transmission occurs.

claims.text: Recurrences and subclinical shedding much more frequent with genital HSV-2 than HSV-1
claims.quote: Recurrences and subclinical shedding are much more frequent for HSV-2 genital herpes infection than for HSV-1 genital herpes

claims.text: Genital HSV-1 recurrences less frequent; shedding decreases rapidly during the first year
claims.quote: Recurrences are less frequent after the first episode of HSV-1 genital herpes, compared with genital HSV-2 genital herpes, and genital shedding rapidly decreases during the first year of infection

claims.text: No data on suppressive therapy for preventing HSV-1 transmission; HSV-1 suppression reserved for frequent recurrences by shared decision-making
claims.quote: No data are available regarding the efficacy of suppressive therapy for preventing transmission among persons with HSV-1 genital herpes infection ... suppressive therapy for HSV-1 genital herpes should be reserved for those with frequent recurrences through shared clinical decision-making

claims.text: People with mild or infrequent outbreaks can benefit; options should be discussed with everyone
claims.quote: Certain persons, including those with mild or infrequent recurrent outbreaks, benefit from antiviral therapy; therefore, options for treatment should be discussed.

claims.text: Daily suppressive therapy (not episodic) is the approach that also lowers the risk of transmitting HSV-2 to partners
claims.quote: Many persons prefer suppressive therapy, which has the additional advantage of decreasing the risk for transmitting HSV-2 genital herpes to susceptible partners

claims.text: NAAT is the most sensitive test; culture sensitivity is low, especially for recurrent lesions, and declines as lesions heal
claims.quote: HSV NAAT assays are the most sensitive tests ... The sensitivity of viral culture is low, especially for recurrent lesions, and decreases rapidly as lesions begin to heal

claims.text: Appearance alone is unreliable; genital ulcers can be caused by syphilis, chancroid and other infections, and noninfectious causes such as trauma
claims.quote: Less common infectious causes of genital, anal, or perianal ulcers include chancroid ... (e.g., yeast, trauma, carcinoma ... A diagnosis based only on medical history and physical examination frequently can be inaccurate.

claims.text: Antibodies develop during the first weeks; repeat testing 12 weeks after suspected recent acquisition
claims.quote: Both type-specific and type-common antibodies to HSV develop during the first weeks after infection ... in cases of recent suspected HSV-2 acquisition, repeat type-specific antibody testing 12 weeks after the presumed time of acquisition is indicated

claims.text: CDC does not recommend HSV-2 serologic screening of the general population
claims.quote: HSV-2 serologic screening among the general population is not recommended.

claims.text: Serology indications: recurrent or atypical symptoms with negative PCR or culture, clinical diagnosis without lab confirmation, partner has genital herpes
claims.quote: useful in the following scenarios: recurrent or atypical genital symptoms or lesions with a negative HSV PCR or culture result, clinical diagnosis of genital herpes without laboratory confirmation, and a patient’s partner has genital herpes

claims.text: Serology in pregnancy for a woman with no history whose partner has HSV; considered for persons with HIV at initial evaluation
claims.quote: such testing might be offered to a woman with no history of genital herpes whose sex partner has HSV infection ... HSV-2 type-specific serologic testing can be considered for persons with HIV infection during their initial evaluation

claims.text: HerpeSelect often falsely positive at index 1.1 to 3.0; specificity 39.8% at 1.1 to 2.9; confirmatory Biokit or Western blot below 3.0
claims.quote: often is falsely positive at low index values (1.1–3.0) ... a specificity of 39.8% for index values of 1.1–2.9 ... particularly with low index values (<3.0), a confirmatory test (Biokit or Western blot) with a second method should be performed

claims.text: New genital herpes can cause prolonged illness with severe ulcers and neurologic involvement; all first episodes should receive antiviral therapy
claims.quote: Newly acquired genital herpes can cause a prolonged clinical illness with severe genital ulcerations and neurologic involvement ... all patients with first episodes of genital herpes should receive antiviral therapy.

claims.text: Valacyclovir better absorbed than acyclovir allowing less frequent dosing; famciclovir high oral bioavailability
claims.quote: Valacyclovir is the valine ester of acyclovir and has enhanced absorption after oral administration, allowing for less frequent dosing than acyclovir. Famciclovir also has high oral bioavailability.

claims.text: IV then oral to complete more than 10 days total; longer for CNS complications
claims.quote: IV therapy should be considered until clinical improvement followed by oral antiviral therapy to complete >10 days of total therapy. Longer duration is recommended for CNS complications.

claims.text: Suppression reduces recurrences 70-80% with frequent recurrences; often no outbreaks; also effective with less frequent recurrences
claims.quote: Suppressive therapy reduces frequency of genital herpes recurrences by 70%–80% among patients who have frequent recurrences ... Persons receiving such therapy often report having experienced no symptomatic outbreaks. Suppressive therapy also is effective for patients with less frequent recurrences.

claims.text: Discuss annually; no discontinuation or lab monitoring needed because adverse events and resistance uncommon
claims.quote: Providers should discuss with patients on an annual basis whether they want to continue suppressive therapy ... neither treatment discontinuation nor laboratory monitoring is necessary because adverse events and development of HSV antiviral resistance related to long-term antiviral use are uncommon

claims.text: Famciclovir appears somewhat less effective for suppressing viral shedding
claims.quote: Famciclovir appears somewhat less effective for suppression of viral shedding

claims.text: Acyclovir 400 mg three times daily for 5 days (episodic) effective but not recommended
claims.quote: Acyclovir 400 mg orally 3 times/day for 5 days is also effective but is not recommended because of frequency of dosing.

claims.text: Prodrome: pain or burning at the site before a lesion appears
claims.quote: prodromal symptoms (e.g., pain or burning at site before appearance of lesion)

claims.text: Discordant couples encouraged to consider suppressive therapy in addition to consistent condom use and avoiding sex during recurrences (also the combined-strategy table row)
claims.quote: Such couples should be encouraged to consider suppressive antiviral therapy as part of a strategy for preventing transmission, in addition to consistent condom use and avoidance of sexual activity during recurrences.

claims.text: Shedding most frequent in the first 12 months after acquiring HSV-2
claims.quote: asymptomatic viral shedding is most frequent during the first 12 months after acquiring HSV-2

claims.text: Condoms used consistently and correctly reduce but do not eliminate transmission risk
claims.quote: The effectiveness of male latex condoms, which when used consistently and correctly can reduce, but not eliminate, the risk for genital herpes transmission

claims.text: Abstain with uninfected partners when lesions or prodromal symptoms present (CDC counseling recommendation)
claims.quote: The importance of abstaining from sexual activity with uninfected partners when lesions or prodromal symptoms are present.

claims.text: Inform current partners and future partners before a sexual relationship
claims.quote: The importance of informing current sex partners about genital herpes and informing future partners before initiating a sexual relationship.

claims.text: Asymptomatic partners asked about symptoms and offered type-specific HSV-2 serology
claims.quote: Asymptomatic sex partners of patients who have symptomatic genital herpes should be asked about a history of genital symptoms and offered type-specific serologic testing for HSV-2.

claims.text: No PEP or PrEP with antivirals for uninfected partners; should not be offered
claims.quote: For partners without genital herpes, no data are available on which to base a recommendation for PEP or PrEP with antiviral medications or that they would prevent acquisition, and this should not be offered to patients as a prevention strategy.

claims.text: All persons with genital herpes should be tested for HIV; HSV-2 increases HIV acquisition risk twofold to threefold
claims.quote: HSV-2 genital herpes infection increases the risk for acquiring HIV twofold to threefold; therefore, all persons with genital herpes should be tested for HIV

claims.text: Neonatal transmission 30% to 50% when acquired near delivery; under 1% with prenatal history of recurrent herpes or acquisition in first half of pregnancy
claims.quote: high (30%–50%) among women who acquire genital herpes near the time of delivery and low (<1%) among women with prenatal histories of recurrent herpes or who acquire genital herpes during the first half of pregnancy

claims.text: Suppression from 36 weeks reduces cesarean by reducing recurrences at term; might not prevent neonatal transmission in all cases
claims.quote: Suppressive acyclovir treatment starting at 36 weeks’ gestation reduces the frequency of cesarean delivery ... by diminishing the frequency of recurrences at term ... such treatment might not protect against transmission to neonates in all cases

claims.text: Acyclovir believed safe in all trimesters; valacyclovir prenatal data limited, animal data indicate low risk
claims.quote: believed to be safe for use during all trimesters of pregnancy ... data regarding prenatal exposure to valacyclovir and famciclovir are limited, data from animal trials indicate that these drugs also pose a low risk among pregnant women

claims.text: Cesarean for recurrent lesions at onset of labor, does not eliminate risk; vaginal delivery without symptoms or prodrome
claims.quote: Women without symptoms or signs of genital herpes or its prodrome can deliver vaginally. Although cesarean delivery does not eliminate the risk ... women with recurrent genital herpetic lesions at the onset of labor should have a cesarean delivery

claims.text: Acquisition in second half of pregnancy managed with maternal-fetal medicine and infectious disease specialists (pregnancy section and red flag)
claims.quote: Women who acquire HSV in the second half of pregnancy should be managed in consultation with maternal-fetal medicine and infectious disease specialists.

claims.text: HSV hepatitis in pregnancy: fever, markedly elevated transaminases, may have no lesions; IV acyclovir
claims.quote: Pregnant women in any trimester can present with fever and hepatitis (markedly elevated transaminases) but might not have any genital or skin lesions ... empiric IV acyclovir should be initiated pending confirmation

claims.text: Routine HSV-2 serologic screening of pregnant women not recommended
claims.quote: Routine HSV-2 serologic screening of pregnant women is not recommended.

claims.text: HSV lesions common, possibly severe, painful, atypical in HIV; shedding increased
claims.quote: Lesions caused by HSV are common among persons with HIV infection and might be severe, painful, and atypical (). HSV shedding is increased among persons with HIV infection

claims.text: HIV first-episode treatment same, courses might need extending
claims.quote: Recommended therapy for first-episode genital herpes is the same as for persons without HIV infection, although treatment courses might need to be extended for lesion resolution.

claims.text: GUD risk rises in first 6 months after ART, especially CD4 below 200; suppression reduces it and can be continued 6 months
claims.quote: The risk for GUD increases during the first 6 months after starting ART, especially among persons who have a CD4T-cell count <200 cell/mm. Suppressive antiviral therapy reduces the risk for GUD ... can be continued for 6 months

claims.text: In HIV/HSV, suppression does not reduce HIV or HSV-2 transmission and does not delay HIV progression on ART
claims.quote: Suppressive antiviral therapy among persons with HIV and HSV infection does not reduce the risk for either HIV transmission or HSV-2 transmission to susceptible sex partners (,). Suppressive antiviral therapy does not delay HIV disease progression

claims.text: Red flag: headache, light sensitivity, fever, stiff neck suggest HSV meningitis needing IV acyclovir
claims.quote: HSV-2 meningitis is characterized clinically by signs of headache, photophobia, fever, meningismus ... acyclovir 5–10 mg/kg body weight IV every 8 hours until clinical improvement is observed

claims.text: Red flag: lesions persisting or recurring on treatment suggest acyclovir resistance; specialist care
claims.quote: If lesions persist or recur in a patient receiving antiviral treatment, acyclovir resistance should be suspected ... Such persons should be managed in consultation with an infectious disease specialist

claims.text: Red flag: babies with neonatal herpes need prompt evaluation and IV acyclovir
claims.quote: All newborn infants who have neonatal herpes should be promptly evaluated and treated with systemic acyclovir. The recommended regimen ... is acyclovir 20 mg/kg body weight IV every 8 hours

claims.text: Red flag: disseminated herpes (hepatitis, pneumonitis) requires hospital care and IV acyclovir
claims.quote: should be provided for patients who have severe HSV disease or complications that necessitate hospitalization (e.g., disseminated infection, pneumonitis, or hepatitis)

claims.text: FAQ: antivirals do not eradicate latent virus
claims.quote: these drugs neither eradicate latent virus nor affect the risk, frequency, or severity of recurrences after the drug is discontinued

claims.text: Virus becomes latent in the sensory ganglion
claims.quote: Following infection, the virus becomes latent in the local sensory ganglion

claims.text: Most people on suppressive therapy still have an occasional recurrence
claims.quote: the majority of patients on such a regimen will still experience an occasional symptomatic recurrence

claims.text: Genital HSV-1 can be acquired through receptive oral sex
claims.quote: Pregnant women should be advised of the risk of acquiring HSV‐1 as a result of receptive orogenital contact

claims.text: Swab from the lesion base; early testing more likely to detect virus
claims.quote: swabs should be taken from the base of the lesion (vesicles should be unroofed with a needle or scalpel blade) (1, A).Viral detection in early disease (for both first episodes and recurrences) are much more likely to be successful

claims.text: First episode: systemic symptoms, local adenitis; presentation depends on prior infection; urinary retention or meningism can require hospitalization
claims.quote: there may be systemic symptoms ... the actual clinical presentation may depend upon previous HSV‐1 or HSV‐2 infection ... Hospitalization may be required for urinary retention, meningism, severe constitutional symptoms

claims.text: Start first-episode therapy at earliest opportunity on clinical suspicion alone
claims.quote: Therapy can be highly effective and should be instigated at the earliest opportunity and on clinical suspicion alone (1,A).

claims.text: Stopping allows reassessment; many find little change; safe to restart
claims.quote: Discontinuation of therapy at this time, if the patient is willing, will allow a reassessment of recurrence frequency ... It is safe and reasonable to restart treatment

claims.text: Many patients find no significant change after discontinuation
claims.quote: many patients do not find a significant alteration in disease frequency or severity upon discontinuation and reassessment

claims.text: No fixed threshold: early trials in about 6 or more recurrences a year; benefit across spectrum; decision balances frequency, impact, transmission
claims.quote: The majority of early trials of suppressive therapy were done in patients with a recurrence rate equivalent to ≥6 recurrences/annum ... patients across all spectrums of disease will benefit ... needs to balance the frequency of recurrence, the impact of disease

claims.text: Episodic therapy shortens outbreaks by a median of 1 to 2 days
claims.quote: The reduction in duration is a median of 1–2 days (1, A).

claims.text: No advantage of 5-day courses over ultra-short courses
claims.quote: Head‐to‐head studies of their effects show no advantage of one therapy over another or the advantage of extended 5‐day treatment over ultra‐short therapy.

claims.text: Transmission risk greatest during recurrences or prodrome; can occur without lesions via subclinical shedding (text and table row)
claims.quote: Risk of transmission appears to be greatest during lesional recurrences or prodrome ... Transmission can occur in the absence of lesional recurrence as a result of sub‐clinical viral shedding.

claims.text: Disclosure advice practical and tailored; frank about subclinical shedding and limited impact of condoms and antivirals
claims.quote: Advice on disclosure should be practical and tailored to the patient's personal situation ... It is important to be frank about transmission risks including subclinical shedding and the limited impact of condoms and antivirals.

claims.text: Distress common, persists, may be reduced by antivirals; depression; withdrawal from relationships for fear of disclosure
claims.quote: High distress at diagnosis is common, often persists with recurrences and may be reduced by antivirals ... can develop symptoms of depression ... Fear of disclosure may be an important contributor to withdrawal from intimate relationships

claims.text: Suppression from 36 weeks should be offered to all women with a history of genital herpes
claims.quote: Daily suppressive aciclovir 400 mg three times a day from 36 weeks gestation should therefore be offered to all women with a history of genital herpes (1, A).

claims.text: Third-trimester first episode: cesarean considered, particularly symptoms within 6 weeks of delivery, high shedding risk
claims.quote: Caesarean section should be considered for all women, particularly those developing symptoms within 6 weeks of delivery, as the risk of viral shedding in labour is very high (1, A).

claims.text: First or second trimester first episode managed per clinical condition with oral or IV acyclovir; vaginal delivery anticipated
claims.quote: Management of the woman should be in line with her clinical condition and will often involve the use of either oral or intravenous aciclovir ... Providing that delivery does not ensue ... vaginal delivery anticipated

claims.text: Sequential PCR in late pregnancy to predict shedding not indicated
claims.quote: Sequential PCR during late gestation to predict viral shedding at term is not indicated.

claims.text: Herpes activates HIV replication and may facilitate HIV transmission
claims.quote: Herpes simplex infections activate HIV replication and may facilitate onward HIV transmission to sexual partners.

claims.text: Suppressive therapy has no impact on HIV acquisition or transmission risk
claims.quote: Suppressive antiviral therapy with currently available agents has been shown in multiple studies to have no impact on HIV acquisition or transmission risk.

claims.text: Recurrences self-limiting with minor symptoms; antivirals shorten them
claims.quote: Genital herpes recurrences are self‐limiting and generally cause minor symptoms ... Oral aciclovir, valaciclovir and famciclovir are effective at reducing the duration and severity of recurrent genital herpes.

claims.text: Disseminated disease in immunocompromised: fulminant hepatitis, pneumonia, multifocal mucocutaneous lesions
claims.quote: progressive, multifocal, and coalescing mucocutaneous anogenital lesions. claims.text: Red flag: urinary retention can need hospital care
